body:
For reference, the following PR implemented this functionality: #96959 

The third level is explained as:
> One that also works normally, but where languages have already been terminated.

But clearly it was not working normally since it was causing a hang.

I guess the behavior implemented in this PR was the intent? @RandomShaper

Yeah, there is some contradiction. In the code there's also these comments on the runlevels:
```
		RUNLEVEL_PRE_EXIT_LANGUAGES, // Block adding new tasks
		RUNLEVEL_EXIT_LANGUAGES, // All threads detach from scripting threads.
```

But the code is blocking new tasks on `RUNLEVEL_EXIT_LANGUAGES`. So, I'm wondering if the blocking loop is simply incorrect.

Fixing the loop condition won't fix the deadlock, though. The render server (or any worker thread processing some task) might still be trying to post a new task and run into the same deadlock (main thread waiting for idle, worker thread being blocked from posting new task).

So, I see it as two (or three) separate issues:
- When are we blocking external threads from adding new tasks.
- How to handle worker threads adding new task, while external threads are blocked.
- (There is a third issue, where a worker thread might report idling but then gets assigned a new task from another not-yet-idling workder thread, invalidating the invariant of the idle counter).

This PR is for the second issue. The other two might be out of scope for this PR.
